page: OVHcloud b3-8 is a general-purpose virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs, meaning hyperthreading is disabled with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a local 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the network configuration lists a baseline bandwidth of 0 Gbps. Additionally, the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a mixed performance profile. The AMD EPYC processor demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests show average results for large-block read and write operations, but small-block cached reads are weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Similarly, Passmark CPU and memory scores, along with database operations and Redis SET operations, rank in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput is limited, falling into the bottom 10% with a rate of 2.76 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the instance achieves average text generation speeds of 138.37 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, but performance drops significantly on larger models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the b3-8 instance offers a dedicated hardware allocation at an entry-level resource density. Because the vCPUs are dedicated rather than shared, it avoids the noisy-neighbor issues common in burstable instances, though its overall compute and memory limits restrict it to lighter workloads. It is best suited for general-purpose applications that require predictable CPU performance but do not demand high memory or storage throughput. Suitable workloads include basic web serving, lightweight background processing, small-scale development environments, and simple utility services.
